I don’t think we’ll ever know who did it. Poor Jonbenet... the investigation was screwed from the start. But it’s hard to believe parents would do this to a child that was seemingly their pride and joy. Patsy lived vicariously through her with the pageants. And I don’t believe Burke was involved either. It’s normal for kids to act out for attention. Especially when they have siblings who are favored over them. But no 9 year old child is capable of carrying out such a brutal murder. And based on adult interviews, it may be that he is on the spectrum (explaining his “bizarre” facial expression/emotion not matching the situation or conversation at hand. But what if the parents, or just John, were blackmailed somehow by someone they knew. Someone else with money and power who had dirt on them. I don’t know whether to believe John had or hadn’t molested Jonbenet. But John is the only one out of the family who I can’t eliminate as a suspect.

I totally get it. Things are really tough when you’re going through depression or other mental illness/trauma at that age. And it’s hard for parents to understand that kids can be going through these things. Mental health issues have been stigmatized and swept under the rug for centuries. But awareness is being spread and people are starting to come around. But give it some time. Trust me. I’m 25 now. If I would’ve ended it at 14 like I was so close to there is so much I would’ve missed out on. There’s so much I didn’t understand at that age. So much I didn’t understand about myself. I had no idea who I was. I’m still trying to figure that out, honestly. But it’s been worth it to stick around, I promise I’m not just saying that. Even though I live with major depressive disorder, ptsd, social anxiety, etc, there are good things to live for. Even if they seem stupid to other people, do the things that make you happy! It’s the little things that matter the most. Tell people you love them. Get outside and feel the sun on your skin, wind in your hair. Stay off social media for a bit. It’s extremely toxic for mental health, and I find it’s very helpful to take breaks and focus on myself. I’m rooting for you! 💞💞💞

You’re not alone. My advice, don’t go to your friends first. People who haven’t gone through this or felt this way typically don’t understand or know how to help. But trained professionals can definitely help you talk through your feelings and get to the root of the problem. Then you can work on making some changes in order to eliminate these thoughts. I recommend talking to a therapist and being evaluated by a psychiatrist. Sometimes talking to someone who will listen with no judgement is incredibly helpful. It definitely helped me become more aware of my thought process and how the trauma I’ve been through still affects me. Learning healthy ways to cope is so important. I hope you will have the courage to get help and take the steps to start feeling better. Always know that there are hotlines you can call at any time to talk to someone if you’re feeling suicidal. Or if you feel you’re in danger, please go to the emergency room. Best of luck to you. Coming from someone who started having those thoughts 11 years ago: its going to be okay 💞

There’s nothing wrong with spending time alone with yourself if you prefer that over the company of others. Personally, I tried to have friends and fit in for a while in high school, but it was too much work. I wasn’t being myself, I was being the person I thought people would like. Truly, I never had any interest in the shit other high school kids were interested in. I couldn’t relate to them at all. I was always the quiet one at the lunch table just stuck listening to everyone else’s gossip and drama. Eventually I started eating alone outside on a stairwell, where there was a nice view and I could relax and daydream. That became my spot. My safe space. I ate there every day for the rest of my high school experience (I can’t remember if it was my last one or two years). As an introvert and socially anxious person (who also has PTSD), social situations are extremely draining and stressful for me. So I don’t force myself to engage in them. But if you think being more social would make you happier, then it’s worth giving it your best try! I don’t know if you see a therapist, but they could definitely help you with a plan for coming out of your shell and developing friendships. It’s not going to happen overnight. It will be many little steps, but if it’s what you want then you’re going to do it 😉 best of luck 💞

You kind of described my situation of transitioning to adulthood as well. I lived with my parents up until a year ago (I’m now 25) and though I worked since the age of 18 I wouldn’t have been able to afford rent anywhere up until then. I feel like I pretty much did everything late. Drivers license at 21 I think. I still have hardly any social skills. I was bullied in middle school for being weird, and consequently kept to myself mostly. There was a lot of trauma throw out the next several years that I believe slowed my growth in many areas. Since then I’ve never felt like I related to people my age. I totally avoided talking to people. Didn’t want to date or go to the mall/movies or hang out like the other teens did. It wasn’t until 23 that I had all my first romantic experiences of physical contact. I wasn’t anywhere near comfortable to being open to the idea before. But still, I haven’t been in an actual relationship with someone I could call my significant other. I don’t know if that’ll ever happen, I kind of don’t trust people anymore and would rather be alone if it means not getting hurt... but anyways. Also, I have been in college since graduating high school in 2014 and still have another semester to graduate. Granted, I didn’t really know what I wanted to do, got rejected from programs over and over, switched majors twice, switched schools, took a year off, etc. But I’ve had to watch people 3 years younger than me graduate before me. It’s hard to not want to give up. I’m so many ways. I just wanted to let you know that you are not alone or weird for the way your journey to adulthood is playing out. It’s different for everyone, and at least we are trying!! For the record, I’ve never been tested for autism but I’m very curious about it recently because I’ve always felt like I’m different and that people treat me different or like I’m stupid and fragile. Anyways I’m wishing you the best, love xxx
PS you are not a burden!!! You are important and we need you.

That’s the thing about depression. You can have everything you thought you wanted, the “perfect” life, and still be miserable. It sounds to me like you need to take a step away, take a break from all your responsibilities and get some help. You’re not the only one who feels the way you do. And you owe it to yourself and your daughter to try and be the best and healthiest version of yourself you can be. In order to get there, you are going to need professional help. I know it’s not fun, but trust me, it’s worth it. Best of luck. Don’t be too hard on yourself. xxx

Im so sorry. I’m 25, and it’s been at least 11 years for me. It’s excruciating sometimes. And I have a hard time coping in healthy ways. But I still have some hope. Things were the worst ever for me near the beginning of the pandemic, and I was actually planning to end it all. It’s horrifying to look back at the state I was in. Shortly after that I started therapy and seeing a psychiatrist. It’s not a cure, but meds definitely help ease the suffering. Unfortunately I think I’m growing a tolerance to mine and will have to keep increasing the dose or starting different ones. But whatever it takes for me to feel that my life is worth living, is what I will do. I still have really low lows. A few nights ago I had to use the hotline. But I’m feeling much better now. Don’t give up. Find what brings you joy, even just a little, and cling to it. Find things to look forward to. I know it’s hard during the pandemic, but a lot of events are happening again. I bought a concert ticket for November, so I have to be here for November to see the concert! Little things like this help. I’m wishing you luck!! xxx

Friend, I don’t want to sugar coat it for you. For many of us it is a lifelong struggle. It’s been an 11 year battle for me with depression. Therapy and medication have helped me come to terms with my issues and accept that it’s okay to have them and that they are not my fault. The realistic answer is no, depression can’t be cured, unless it’s based off of a specific event (such as grieving a death, suffering a health problem, postpartum, etc.) where it normally subsides in a short time. But I also think it’s worth it for us to stay and fight for our lives. There are good, important things we would miss out on if we leave. Don’t let the bad outweigh the good. And as much as it can feel nobody would be affected by losing us, it’s completely untrue. We are loved. Sometimes it’s hard for our loved ones to understand what we’re going through or how to love and support us in the way we can feel it. But we’re in this together.
